findings.title: 18 broken links: the site links to addresses that answer an error
findings.why: A visitor who follows one of these links reaches an error instead of the page promised.
findings.fix: Point each link at a page that exists, or bring the page back (or redirect its old address to where it went).

findings.title: 6 links to other sites lead nowhere: the pages are gone

link.answer: no answer in time, asked twice

findings.why: Sites move and close: a visitor who follows one of these links meets an error page, or nothing at all, on someone else's site, and leaves thinking less of this one.
findings.fix: Point each link at where the page lives now, or take it out. The suite's link report asks every one again on each run, and fails when one that answered stops.

findings.title: 35 links and buttons on 29 pages have nothing for a screen reader to say
findings.why: A blind visitor hears only "link" or "button", with no idea where it goes or what it does; accessibility law (the ADA, the European Accessibility Act) counts it, and so do automated accessibility audits.
findings.fix: Give each one words: visible text, an aria-label, or an alt on the image inside it (an icon link to a cart: aria-label="Cart").

findings.title: 25 form fields on 22 pages have no label
findings.why: A screen reader announces a field with no label as "edit text", so a blind visitor cannot tell what to type; a placeholder alone vanishes once typing starts. Accessibility audits fail it.
findings.fix: Give each field a <label for="its id"> (each id used once on the page), or an aria-label.

findings.why: On a phone a page with no viewport setting is drawn at desktop width and shrunk to fit, and Google ranks it as not mobile-friendly. A page that stops zooming fails people who need larger text (WCAG 1.4.4).
findings.fix: Use <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">, without user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1.

findings.title: 129 scripts, style sheets and data requests on 45 pages failed to load
findings.why: A script or style sheet that does not load leaves part of the page unstyled or not working: a menu that does not open, a button that does nothing, a list that never fills. Visitors see it; nothing tells the site's owner.
findings.fix: Point each at a file that exists (a path changed in a release is the usual cause), or remove the reference.

findings.why: An error nothing catches stops the script that threw it: whatever it was doing (a form's checks, a cart, tracking) is left undone. Visitors never report it; it is seen only in the browser's console.
findings.fix: Open the page with the browser's developer tools, read the console, and fix each error at the line it names.

findings.title: 6 of the site's own links redirect before they arrive
findings.why: Every click on one of these links costs an extra round trip before the page starts loading, and search engines see one page at two addresses.
findings.fix: Link to each page's final address (with or without its trailing slash, as the server serves it).

findings.title: 4 different pages share one title
findings.why: Search results, bookmarks and browser tabs show the title: pages that share one can't be told apart, and a page without one shows its address.
findings.fix: Give each page a title of its own that names what it shows (in a single-page app, set it on each route).

findings.title: 1 image on 1 page has no alt text
findings.why: A screen reader reads the file name instead, or nothing; search engines lose the words that say what the image shows.
findings.fix: Add alt="what the image shows"; for an image that is decoration only, alt="".

findings.title: 2 pages have no main heading; 4 pages have several main headings (h1)

where.says: 2 h1: `NEWSROOM`, `True Classic Avoids an Inbound Supply Chain Disruption on DTC and B2B with Stord`
2 h1: `NEWSROOM`, `goodr Partners with Stord to Deliver Exceptional Fulfillment Experiences at Scal`
2 h1: `NEWSROOM`, `Stord Leadership Talks Beating Amazon Prime and the Future of AI-Powered Fulfill`

findings.why: Screen reader users jump to the h1 to learn what a page is, and search engines read it as the page's subject; none, or several competing, says neither.
findings.fix: Give each page one h1 naming what it shows; the site's name in the header is not it.

findings.title: 3 pages have no description for search results; 11 pages share one

where.says: shares `Get a custom omnichannel fulfillment, freight, and/or sof...`
shares `Get a custom omnichannel fulfillment, freight, and/or sof...`
shares `Get a custom omnichannel fulfillment, freight, and/or sof...`

findings.why: Search results show the description under the title; without one, the search engine picks a line of the page, often the menu or a cookie notice.
findings.fix: Give each page a <meta name="description"> of a sentence or two saying what it offers.

findings.title: 3 security headers no page sends

where.says: no page of the site sends Content-Security-Policy (which scripts may run)
no page of the site sends X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors (another site cannot frame it to trick a click)
no page of the site sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

findings.why: Each header closes a door attackers use (a downgrade to http, a script slipped in, the site framed in another to trick a click). Security reviews and compliance checklists ask for them, and they cost a line of server configuration.
findings.fix: Add the missing headers in the web server or the CDN (one setting each), starting with Strict-Transport-Security.

findings.title: Requests to 1 host of other sites failed during the crawl, as seen from the crawler's machine and network

where.says: `api.unifyintent.com`: 71 pages asked it for data and the request failed (401); the name resolves from here, so the request failed for another reason

findings.why: A script on the page asked another site's host for data (a third party's logging, analytics or a widget) and got an error or no answer. This was seen from the crawler's own machine and network only: an ad blocker, the region, DNS filtering or the crawler's own network can cause the same failure, and it may not fail for real visitors. The crawl cannot tell whether a page needs the answer. Where the crawl looked the name up from here, the line says so; "does not resolve" is stronger than "the request failed" (the host is probably gone), but it too is seen from here. It stops no build and no test.
findings.fix: If a name does not resolve, the host is probably gone: remove its snippet or tag from the site. Otherwise open the page from an ordinary browser and network; if the request works there, there is nothing to fix.

findings.title: The site has no security.txt: someone who finds a hole has no way to report it
findings.why: Researchers who find a security problem look for /.well-known/security.txt to know whom to tell (RFC 9116); without it they may not report it, or report it publicly.
findings.fix: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with a Contact line (an email address or a form) and an Expires line.
